label: Original-phase steps 3-5 after a prefix starting with y/0 and rich in {y,0,j,k,2,b}
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at positions t=3-5 (t=4 holds about 65% of activation mass). It never fires at t<3 or in the copy phase, and fires only weakly at the delimiter. Within that window it depends on which tokens came earlier: rates are highest when the first token is y (11.7x lift) or 0 (6.7x), and when the preceding inputs include j, 2, k, y, 0 or b. The strongest activations (~0.9-1.0 of max) are on sequences that open with y 0 / y y / 0 0 followed by j/k/2/b, with the activation landing on the 5th token (often c). The position window alone gets 98% recall but only 2% precision. The best content predicate (first token y/0 and at least two prefix tokens from {y,0,j,k,2,b}) gets dev F1 0.41 and mass recall 0.63. Many sequences match this pattern without the feature firing, and about a third of activation mass sits on other prefix combinations, so this looks like a distributed code over the content of the first ~4 tokens that a simple predicate does not fully capture. The feature is not tied to any particular current input token, although c is somewhat enriched (4.4x).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=y (+7.27), orig0=0 (+6.00), orig1=0 (+4.13), orig1=y (+4.06), prev_tok=j (+3.59), prev2_tok=j (+3.32). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-8.09), t=7 (-7.08), t=6 (-6.54), phase=2 (-5.63).
